items.title: Iran's UN envoy accuses Trump of inciting terrorism

featured_image.name: Iran urges UN to respond to Trump's 'reckless' threats over protests

items.description: Iran's ambassador to the United Nations accused President Donald Trump of inciting terrorism in a letter sent to UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, as the war between the United States and Iran entered its sixth week with a critical deadline looming.

items.title: Iranian drone strike wounds 15 US troops at Kuwait air base

featured_image.name: Around 140 US service members wounded in Iran war, Pentagon says

items.description: An Iranian drone strike on Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait overnight on Sunday wounded 15 American service members, with most having already returned to duty, according to CBS News, citing two US officials with knowledge of the attack. The strike marks the latest in a series of Iranian assaults on US positions in the Gulf since the war began on February 28.[1][2][3]

items.title: Iran-launched drone kills couple in Erbil village

featured_image.name: Huge Fire after Drone Attack Hits Engine Oil Warehouse in Iraqi ...

items.description:
An explosive-laden drone launched from Iran struck a civilian home in the village of Zargazawi in Erbil province early Tuesday, killing a married couple and marking the latest deadly escalation in a weeks-long aerial campaign against Iraq's Kurdistan Region.

The Kurdistan Region's Directorate General of Counter-Terrorism (CTD) confirmed that the drone hit the home at approximately 12:15 a.m. local time on Tuesday in the Dara Shakran sub-district, killing Musa Anwar Rasul and Mujda Asaad Hasan. The CTD condemned the attack as a violation of international law and a war crime. Air defense systems intercepted multiple other drones over Erbil the same night, including at least four targeting the US consulate, according to Shafaq News.[1][2]

items.title: Israel orders evacuation of 41 towns in southern Lebanon

featured_image.name: Israel launches Beirut strikes, orders more evacuations in southern Lebanon

items.description:
The Israeli military issued urgent evacuation orders on Monday evening directing residents of 41 towns and residential clusters in southern Lebanon to move north of the Zahrani River, according to the Qatar News Agency and local Lebanese media. The directive, delivered by the Israeli military's Arabic-language spokesman Colonel Avichay Adraee, came amid a day of intensified airstrikes across southern Lebanon, Beirut's southern suburbs, and areas previously considered safe from bombardment.[1][2]

The orders mark the latest expansion of what Israel has described as a security buffer zone, which has grown from the Litani River northward to the Zahrani River — roughly 40 kilometers from the Israeli border — encompassing nearly 15 percent of Lebanon's total land area.[3][4]

items.title: Iran launches fresh missile barrage at southern Israel

featured_image.name: Iran launches ‘revenge’ missile attack on Israel after assassinations

items.description: Iran fired a new wave of ballistic missiles at southern Israel on Monday, targeting areas including Beersheba, Dimona, and the wider Negev region after a hours-long lull in attacks, as the broader war between Iran and Israel entered its sixth week. The strikes came alongside a coordinated Houthi assault on the Red Sea city of Eilat, marking a new phase of multi-front escalation.

items.title: UN Security Council to vote on Strait of Hormuz resolution

featured_image.name: Iran warns UNSC against 'provocative action' on Hormuz

items.description: The United Nations Security Council is scheduled to vote on Tuesday at 11 a.m. Eastern Time on a watered-down resolution addressing Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, diplomatic sources told AFP, capping weeks of fractious negotiations that saw the original text stripped of its most forceful provisions. The vote comes just nine hours before President Donald Trump's self-imposed deadline for Iran to agree to a deal or face strikes on its power plants and bridges.[1][2][3]

items.title: Saudi Arabia intercepts missiles as debris falls near energy sites

featured_image.name: Saudi Arabia intercepts 7 missiles; debris falls near energy facilities |  Reuters

items.description: Saudi Arabia's defense ministry announced early Tuesday that air defenses intercepted multiple ballistic missiles fired toward the kingdom's Eastern Province, with debris falling near energy facilities. The ministry said damage assessment was underway but did not identify the source of the attack.[1][2]

items.title: Four IDF combat soldiers arrested for suspected Iran espionage

featured_image.name: Israel arrests second group of alleged Iran spies

items.description: Israeli security forces have arrested four active-duty combat soldiers on suspicion of espionage on behalf of Iran, in what officials describe as one of the most serious security cases uncovered since the start of the war. The case is one of three Iran-linked espionage affairs made public on Monday.

items.title: Israel hits Iran's largest petrochemical plant as war escalates

featured_image.name: Iran's top university bombed as US, Israel intensify attacks; 34 killed

items.description: Israel struck the South Pars petrochemical plant at Asaluyeh on Monday, targeting what Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz called "the largest petrochemical facility in Iran," as the U.S.-Israeli military campaign expanded its focus to economic and civilian infrastructure. At least 34 people were killed across Iran on Monday, including six children, according to Iranian officials and media reports.[1][2]

items.title: Iran vows Strait of Hormuz will 'never return' to pre-war state

featured_image.name: Strait of Hormuz becomes site of asymmetric naval war with uncertain outcome

items.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy declared on Monday that the Strait of Hormuz will "never return to its former state" for the United States and Israel, warning it was finalizing operational preparations for what it described as a "new order" in the Persian Gulf. The defiant statement arrived as President Donald Trump's latest deadline for Iran to reopen the strategic waterway was set to expire, with the president threatening devastating strikes on Iranian infrastructure if Tehran continues its blockade.[1][2][3]

items.title: North Korea calls Lee's drone regret 'wise' in rare conciliatory exchange

featured_image.name: Sister of North Korea's leader says South Korea's drone regret was ...

items.description: North Korea on Monday called it "very fortunate and wise" for South Korean President Lee Jae Myung to express regret over unauthorized drone flights into its territory, in a rare conciliatory exchange between the two rivals.[1][2]

items.title: UK bars US from using British bases to strike Iran's civilian infrastructure

featured_image.name: UK authorizes US use of British bases for strikes on Iran ...

items.description: As President Donald Trump's latest deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz approaches on Tuesday evening, the British government has signaled it will not permit the United States to use RAF Fairford or Diego Garcia for strikes on Iranian bridges and power plants, according to a report by The i Paper cited by GB News. The move draws a firm line between the defensive operations Britain has already authorized and the sweeping campaign against civilian infrastructure that Trump threatened at a White House press conference on Monday.[1]

items.title: US confirms 13,000 targets struck in Iran over 38 days of war

featured_image.name: U.S. launched "air armada" to rescue F-15 crew in Iran - Axios

items.description:
U.S. Central Command on Monday released an updated operational fact sheet confirming that American forces have struck more than 13,000 targets across Iran since Operation Epic Fury began on February 28, with more than 155 Iranian naval vessels damaged or destroyed over the course of the campaign.[1][2]

President Donald Trump, speaking to reporters at the White House on Monday, said the U.S. military has conducted more than 10,000 combat flights over Iran in 37 days — a figure he called "unheard of". Trump also acknowledged that an F-15E Strike Eagle shot down last week was the first manned American aircraft lost to enemy fire during the war, though he dismissed the incident, calling it "a lucky hit".[3][4]

items.title: Sanchez calls Middle East leaders, demands end to Iran war

featured_image.name: Spanish premier links 'illegal' Iran war to wider Middle East conflicts  ahead of EU summit

items.description:
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Monday conducted a flurry of phone calls with leaders across the Middle East, pressing for an immediate end to the war that has engulfed the region since the United States and Israel launched strikes on Iran in late February.

Sanchez spoke with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, Jordan's King Abdullah II, Qatar's Amir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, and Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam, according to statements from all four governments.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: Artemis II crew restores contact after 40-minute blackout, begins Earth return

featured_image.name: Artemis II live updates as crew comes back into contact ...

items.description:
NASA's Artemis II crew restored contact with Mission Control on Monday evening after a planned 40-minute communications blackout caused by the Orion spacecraft passing behind the far side of the Moon. The blackout, which began at approximately 6:44 p.m. ET, ended around 7:25 p.m. when the spacecraft emerged and NASA's Deep Space Network reacquired the signal.[1][2]

"Integrity, we have you," Mission Control said as contact was reestablished. Mission specialist Christina Koch replied, "Houston, we have you the same and it is so great to hear from Earth again".[2]

items.title: Gulf states intercept fresh Iranian missiles, drones across four countries

featured_image.name: Saudi Arabia Intercepts 7 Missiles Targeting Riyadh, Downs 10 ...

items.description: Air defense systems across the Persian Gulf fired through the night and into Monday morning as Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and Kuwait engaged a fresh wave of Iranian missiles and drones, extending a campaign of aerial attacks that has tested allied defenses daily since late February.

items.title: UN issues urgent call for aid as Cuba crisis worsens

featured_image.name: Cuba is entirely without power following electric grid collapse

items.description:
The United Nations issued an urgent call for international support on Monday as Cuba's energy crisis continues to worsen, with blackouts lasting 18 or more hours a day leaving millions without power across the island nation.[1][2]

UN Resident Coordinator Francisco Pichon, briefing reporters in New York from Havana, said the humanitarian situation has "worsened" since the end of March despite the recent arrival of limited fuel supplies, including a Russian tanker carrying roughly 700,000 barrels of crude oil that the United States allowed through its blockade last week. An updated UN Action Plan aims to support around two million people across eight provinces, but a funding gap of $68 million remains after $26.2 million has already been mobilized.[3][1]

items.title: Pakistan demands Taliban declare TTP a terrorist group

featured_image.name: Chinese officials and Taliban meet, in sign of warming ties

items.description:
Pakistan has formally presented three demands to Afghanistan's Taliban government as preconditions for resolving the ongoing cross-border conflict: that Kabul declare the Tehrik-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) a terrorist organization, dismantle its infrastructure inside Afghanistan, and provide verifiable proof of those actions through independent monitoring.[1][2]

The demands were conveyed during China-mediated talks in Urumqi last week, marking the first major diplomatic engagement since Pakistan launched Operation Ghazab lil-Haq in late February, a military campaign targeting what Islamabad described as terrorist hideouts inside Afghan territory.[3][2]

items.title: Zelensky sends energy truce offer to Russia via US mediators

featured_image.name: Zelenskiy says he will ask US to relay Easter energy truce offer to ...

items.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky announced on Monday that Ukraine has conveyed a proposal for a mutual ceasefire on energy infrastructure strikes to Russia through American intermediaries, even as Russian forces launched more than 140 drones overnight in a barrage that killed three people in Odesa, including a mother and her two-year-old daughter.

items.title: Israeli strikes kill at least 10 near Gaza school

featured_image.name: Israeli airstrike kills at least 10 near Gaza school as ceasefire strains |  Reuters

items.description:
At least 10 Palestinians were killed and several others wounded on Monday when Israeli drones fired two missiles near a school sheltering displaced people east of the Maghazi refugee camp in central Gaza, according to health officials and medics cited by Reuters.[1][2]

The strikes came during clashes between Hamas security forces and an Israeli-backed militia that had attacked the school area in what residents described as an abduction attempt. Ahmed al-Maghazi, an eyewitness, told Reuters that residents tried to defend their homes before Israeli forces intervened from the air. "The residents tried to defend their homes, but the occupation forces targeted them directly," he said.[2]
